mechanism: Allocate CPU-visible buffer shadows lazily in 4 KiB pages rather than 64 KiB chunks. Shadow comparison, packet order and native write-tracking protocol are unchanged.
measurementLane: Synthetic actual Device::flush_cpu_buffers native Windows benchmark. No GPU or game data. Each run has matched baseline/patch binaries on one GitHub Actions VM; the supplemental control used a separate VM/CPU.
primaryStatistic: Median of seven samples of elapsed milliseconds per actual flush; allocated shadow payload byte counts are exact and repeatable. CPU time is recorded separately using Windows GetProcessTimes user+kernel.

memoryAccounting.measured: Sum of Resource::shadow_resident_bytes over the benchmark resources: allocated shadow payload only, not process RSS or physical residency.
memoryAccounting.metadataTradeoff: Each 48 KiB buffer requires twelve shadow pointer slots instead of one. At eight bytes per pointer this is 88 additional bytes per buffer, or 352 KiB for 4096 buffers, before allocator/vector overhead. This is a modeled metadata cost, not an RSS measurement.
memoryAccounting.sparseFirstResult: After 64 sparse first-touch flushes, allocated payload falls from 136.5 MiB to 18.25 MiB (118.25 MiB saved, 86.63%).
memoryAccounting.denseResult: Dense workloads allocate the same shadow payload in both variants; page granularity increases allocation count and pointer metadata.

materialTradeoff: The partially resident sparse workload is 17.21% slower (0.101481 ms per flush) while reducing final shadow payload from 192 MiB to 32.5625 MiB. Its initial warmup writes only the first page of each buffer: the baseline has already allocated every neighboring page, while the patch allocates additional pages when first written. This regression is retained, not replaced by the fully resident sparse control.
fullyResidentSparseControl: The separate fully resident sparse control initializes all twelve pages before timing. It measures 0.368512 to 0.373480 ms per flush (+0.004968 ms, +1.35%), with overlapping ranges, on a different CPU from the primary six workloads. Both variants allocate 192 MiB payload.
correctness: Every WriteBuffer payload, destination offset and resource order checked outside timing.
Packet digest, visited/skipped counts, compared bytes, take-range counts and upload counts match baseline and patch for every stored sample of each workload.
Shadow payload metrics are repeatable across all seven samples of each variant/workload.
Focused test_d3d12_xs_exports passes in both Windows runs; regression assertions cover lazy allocation of one, two and three independent pages, zero rewrites, alias/window marks and remaps.

reproduction.shell: PowerShell on Windows with MSVC Visual Studio 2022 and CMake; run from a clean PR checkout. Baseline benchmark source is copied verbatim from the patch and uses baseline public APIs.
commands:
@'
option(PLAYGTA6_PERFORMANCE_BENCHMARKS "Build manual performance probes" OFF)
if(PLAYGTA6_PERFORMANCE_BENCHMARKS)
  add_executable(bench_buffer_shadows ../tests/bench_buffer_shadows.cpp)
  target_link_libraries(bench_buffer_shadows PRIVATE playgta6_core)
endif()
'@ | Add-Content ../shadow-base/runtime/CMakeLists.txt
reproduction.sampling: For each workload execute one untimed invocation per binary, then seven pairs alternating baseline/patch and patch/baseline order. No build or test runs during timing. The program excludes fixture creation, four warmup flushes, guest writes and all correctness/metric collection. Dense-first runs time exactly one flush after every page is first changed, rather than averaging it over resident flushes.

unmeasured: Real-game buffer sizes, write distributions, allocation churn, frame rate and end-to-end gameplay.
Browser/Wasm execution, shared XMem view write tracking, GPU execution and real game assets.
Actual process RSS/working set, allocator metadata/fragmentation and long-running memory behavior.
No claim that the measured milliseconds translate directly into a sustained-FPS increase.

results.benchmark: synthetic actual native Device::flush_cpu_buffers with Windows write tracking; page-sized shadow probe
results.sampling: separate prebuilt MSVC Release binaries; one untimed invocation each, then seven alternating A/B pairs; four warmup flushes per invocation; setup, guest writes, output checks and metric collection excluded from timed flush; dense-first times ONE flush and is not averaged with resident flushes
results.metrics: elapsed wall and GetProcessTimes user+kernel CPU; allocated shadow payload bytes from Resource::shadow_resident_bytes, excluding pointer-vector and allocator metadata; 4KiB pointer slots require up to 12 pointers instead of one per48KiB buffer
results.unmeasured: real game allocation/write distribution, shared XMem views, browser/Wasm, GPU execution, actual process RSS and sustained game FPS
